assessment: BMW ties the production contribution to ten months. Figure describes an 11-month deployment, says full deployment launched within ten months and separately cites six months of daily runtime. The public sources do not define a single common start date or explain the scope difference.

value: “Minimal hardware failures”; forearm identified as top hardware failure point

assessment: Agility describes the commercial workflow as autonomous. No reviewed source separates autonomous execution, supervision, teleoperation, exception handling or recovery time.

value: Multiple Digit robots described; exact deployed count not published
assessment: The commercial announcements use plural language but provide no unit count or unit-level output and runtime distribution.

label: Battery swap

value: 24/7 continuous operation
assessment: Describes intended capability enabled by the battery architecture. It is not measured availability, does not mean uninterrupted task execution and has no stated observation window.

label: Energy architecture
value: Dual-battery hot-swappable system
assessment: The page describes dual- and single-battery modes plus automatic selection between swapping and charging. It provides no measured energy duty cycle or evidence that production work continues through every swap.

label: Commercial maturity
value: Mass production and delivery claimed
assessment: The current product page presents Walker S2 as in mass production and delivery. That commercial-status statement does not supply operator-level runtime or reliability evidence.

label: Autonomy boundary
value: Battery replenishment described as autonomous; task autonomy not measured
assessment: The autonomy claim is specific to battery monitoring, swap or charge selection and the swapping procedure. It does not quantify autonomous task time, supervision, recovery or human intervention in an industrial workflow.

label: Project existence
value: Figure 03 sequencing project at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg
assessment: BMW confirms the robot, site and intended logistics use case. Its announcement is forward-looking and does not establish that routine production operation had begun.

label: Project stage
value: Operator announcement plus manufacturer-described first demonstration
assessment: BMW says Figure 03 will now start on the application; Figure later describes a first demonstration. HumanoidUptime therefore does not classify the record as a quantified field deployment.

label: Task definition
value: Pick parts and sort them into a sequencing trolley for onward transport
assessment: BMW defines parts moving from bulk containers into a sequencing trolley for onward transport. No attempts, completed sequences, throughput or success criterion is published.

label: Control system
value: Helix 02 whole-body control asserted for the demonstration
assessment: Figure describes perception-led corrections and whole-body control, but does not publish an autonomous-time share or separate supervision, teleoperation, resets and recovery.

label: Test configuration
value: G1 EDU-4, Dex3-1 three-finger hands, firmware 1.04
assessment: Fraunhofer identifies the tested configuration and states that the unit was delivered in May 2025; results should not be generalized to other variants or firmware versions without qualification.

label: Energy and endurance
value: 239 W mean power and 1:49 h derived per-charge endurance in the defined typical scenario
assessment: Fraunhofer measures power in standardized standing and walking conditions and derives maximum operating times from those results. The 1:49 figure is not presented as an observed continuous field run or cumulative runtime. Fraunhofer also reports 154 W standing, 272 W level walking, 283 W at 10% incline and a derived 2:49 h for standing only.
source_metric_term: maximum operating time in the typical scenario
metric_interpretation: This is a scenario-derived energy-endurance result. It is valid for the stated laboratory scenario, but it does not measure availability against scheduled operating time.

label: Walking speed
value: 0.49 m/s slow and 0.84 m/s fast walking measured with 3D tracking
assessment: A 3 kg load did not reduce steady walking speed in the described test, but increased acceleration and deceleration time by several tenths of a second.

label: Thermal constraint
value: Outstretched arms could shut down after one to two minutes without added payload
assessment: Fraunhofer attributes the shutdown and dropping arms to actuator overheating. No frequency across repeated trials or recovery time is published.

label: Collision force
value: Mean peak forces of approximately 510 N at the chest and 530 N at the abdomen in specified walking collisions
assessment: Fraunhofer's public safety guide states that displayed values are mean peak forces from at least three trials per scenario with the robot in fast mode at about 1 m/s. It does not publish the underlying observations, spread or unit-to-unit variation.

label: Stability and recovery
value: No balance loss on cable-channel steps or a 20% ramp; recovery depended on floor friction
assessment: Self-stabilization was strong in the described tests, while standing up from the back failed on smooth tile and wood because the arms could slip.

label: Cybersecurity
value: Bluetooth remote-code-execution vulnerability found in the tested software state
assessment: Fraunhofer reports that the vulnerability persisted across several firmware updates and was subsequently closed by a newer update.

label: Delivered autonomy
value: Remote-controlled walking available after delivery; further capabilities require user implementation
assessment: This is the observed baseline of the tested EDU configuration, not a claim about every later software stack built on the platform.

label: Deployment scope
value: Two-week on-site proof of concept at Siemens' electronics factory in Erlangen
assessment: Humanoid specifies the two-phase program and two-week factory period. Siemens independently confirms the factory and operational test, but its later release does not restate the two-week duration.

label: Task
value: Pick totes from a stack, transport them to a conveyor and place them for human operators
assessment: Both parties describe an autonomous tote-handling workflow. Humanoid adds that the sequence repeated until the stack was empty and used two tote sizes.

value: 60 tote moves per hour
assessment: Siemens and Humanoid report that the target was met. Neither publishes the observation count, distribution, pauses or throughput variability.

metric_interpretation: The source uses the word “uptime”, but the published inputs do not support a technical-availability percentage.

label: Continuous autonomous run
value: More than 30 minutes
assessment: This is the only explicitly bounded continuous autonomous interval in the detailed POC account. The source provides no intervention or stop-event log for the interval.

value: Above 90% autonomous pick-and-place success
assessment: Siemens corroborates the autonomous rate. Humanoid additionally says both overall and autonomous rates exceeded 90%, but neither source defines attempts, retries, failures or human-assisted completions.

value: Autonomous execution integrated with the Siemens factory environment
assessment: The task is described as autonomous and Siemens identifies its industrial integration layer. No breakdown of supervised, teleoperated, recovery or autonomous time is published.
